Derivative/reference-rate discontinuation language is accounting/financing rather than customer-product withdrawal.

Rebate and inflation language reflects statutory pricing rules and regulation, not a new company-originated customer action.
Higher ASP from price increases and mix is already explicit at F1 and persists; strong but static existing-customer yield optimization.
Pricing references are primarily regulatory-risk discussion rather than a concrete company action in the frozen trajectory.

Acquisition and LIBOR-migration language is non-qualifying.
Share-repurchase and reference-rate discontinuation language does not affect customers.

Medicare Part D cost-sharing stages are statutory plan-design mechanics rather than a newly company-originated economic action.

Price increases are discussed as pharmaceutical-industry/regulatory conditions rather than an AmerisourceBergen-originated customer action.

The company describes inability to pass higher costs to customers rather than an implemented transfer.
